newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China Dalian refinery offers first export cargoes.
newsitem.headline: China Dalian refinery offers first export cargoes.

text.p: China's largest Sino-foreign joint-venture oil refinery in Dalian has emerged to offer its maiden oil product cargoes for export, an official with state-owned SINOCHEM said on Monday.

The new refinery which began a three-month trial run since early October has one cargo each of gasoline and diesel for sale during second half November, said Yang Chao Feng, products trading manager with SINOCHEM Singapore.
SINOCHEM has a 27.5-percent stake in the 100,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery, also known as the Dalian West Pacific Petrochemical Co (WEPEC), which is jointly owned by several Chinese companies.
Total SA of France holds a 20-percent stake in the plant, which is located in northeast China and was built as an export-oriented refinery.
But Yang said the rest of the products including naphtha, jet fuel and fuel oil would be kept for the Chinese domestic market.
"All depends on world (refining) margins and Chinese domestic prices," Yang said. "If world margins are better, we will export, and if China's prices are good, we will keep the product domestically."
SINOCHEM Singapore, which is marketing the products from the refinery, is offering up to 30,000 tonnes each of diesel and gasoline.
The low sulphur diesel has the typical guarantee of 0.1-percent sulphur although the refinery actually produces the 0.05-to-0.06-percent sulphur grade.
For the gasoline, SINOCHEM guarantees a sulphur content of 0.014 percent and an oxygenate number of 90 although the refinery is capable of producing 91 to 92 octane unleaded material, Yang said.
He said the aromatic and benzene content could not be guaranteed as the gasoline was a mix from the refinery's reforming and cracking units.
"It is not the typical spec (specification) ... that is the problem," he said as the gasoline grade does not match the South Korean market requirements which SINOCHEM is targetting.
SINOCHEM prefers to sell the gasoline cargo based on Singapore spot quotes for 93-octane unleaded on a free-on-board (fob) basis. But no firm bids or offers have been made, he said.
Yang said SINOCHEM plans to sell some products on term contract basis although no discussions are due before the end of the three-month test run period.
